lesson_title: Tidy First: Why 2x + 3x Is Not a Binomial
hook_text: 2x plus 3x. Two pieces, so a binomial? Wrong — and the reason is the whole lesson.
clip_script: Count the pieces between the plus and minus signs. One piece, monomial — like monorail. Two, binomial — bicycle. Three, trinomial — tricycle. 4x cubed: one. x squared minus 9: two. 3x squared minus 5x plus 2: three. Easy. Now the trap. 2x plus 3x — two pieces? No. They are the same fruit, so they collapse to 5x. One piece. Monomial. Tidy the room BEFORE you count what is in it. Times signs do not make gaps either: 3xy is one piece with three ingredients. Then add the first name: biggest power 1 is linear, 2 is quadratic, 3 is cubic. 3x squared minus 5x plus 2 is a quadratic trinomial. 4x cubed is a cubic monomial — the 3 is its power, not its pieces.
visual_style: Expressions appear as food on a plate with glowing gaps at each plus and minus; 2x and 3x slide together into one piece labelled 5x; a name tag stamps itself onto each expression.
pacing: Fast counting, a hard brake on 2x + 3x, a crisp naming finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and name any expression in two words.
